previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, morbid obesity, chronic diastolic heart failure, type 2 diabetes, and prior DVT/PE was admitted with cough, low-grade fever, and generalized weakness. She had stopped taking warfarin and furosemide at home, and recently reduced her steroid dose. Evaluation revealed no bacterial infection; symptoms were attributed to a viral syndrome with mild acute on chronic heart failure, which improved with a single IV lasix dose and resumption of oral diuretic. A contaminated urine culture with E. coli was treated with a short course of cefpodoxime. Warfarin was restarted using fondaparinux as a bridge due to poor IV access and failed PICC placement. INR reached therapeutic levels by discharge. CellCept was initiated for polymyositis with a planned titration schedule and weekly lab monitoring. She was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs, improved strength, and clear discharge instructions for medication management and follow-up.

ACTIVE ISSUES BY PROBLEM: 
# Polymyositis: presented with her typical symptoms of her 
flares including extremity pain and weakness and an elevated CK 
(3578 vs ~600 in ___, vs peak of 15,827 in ___ during 
her worst flare). She was started initially overnight on high 
dose steroids with methylpred 125 mg IV q8h and continued on 
cellcept 1500mg BID.  Rheumatology consult was obtained, and her 
primary rheumatologist Dr. ___ decreasing her 
steroid dose to IV methyl pred 20 mg daily the following day 
(received ___ doses of 125mg).  She recieved rituxan on ___ 
with no complications.  Her symptoms gradually improved, and her 
CKs trended down (from peak 3909).  Her methylpred was 
transitioned to 20 mg PO, which she continued on discharge and 
will be titrated as an outpatient by her rheumatologist.  She 
has been continued on cellcept 1500mg BID and will have her next 
rituxan dose as an outpatient on ___.  Physical therapy felt 
that she strength had improved to the point that she was able to 
be discharged to home with plans for follow up with PCP and 
rheum 
  
# History of PE on coumadin:  subtherapeutic on admission, 
likely due to her diet changes -- said she was not eating much 
and had been having a lot of salads.  Initially given increased 
dose of coumadin (12mg on admission), but INR crept up to 4.2, 
so coumadin was held for 1 day.  INR came back into therapeutic 
range, and she was discharged on alternating regimen of 7.5mg 
and 10mg every other day. She will have her next INR check on 
___ and follow up in ___ clinic.
  
INACTIVE, CHRONIC ISSUES: 
# Chronic blood loss anemia: Microcytic, MCV ___. Hct from 39 in 
___ to ___ now, stable during admission. Likely ___ her 
ongoing vaginal bleeding, which is followed by OB/gyn (to have 
mirena placed on ___. She was started on ferrous sulfate 325 
mg daily in the interim for her iron deficiency. 
  
# DM: Metformin initially held on admission and started on SSI, 
however metformin was restarted on HD#2 with improvement of 
glucoses.  
   
# Chronic Diastolic CHF with preserved EF:  No evidence of acute 
exacerbation.  On lasix at home. Has slightly worsening of her 
non-pitting edema which she reports is consistent with her 
polymyositis flares. No shortness of breath, and breathing 
comfortably on room air. CXR on admission with mild pulmonary 
edema and trace left effusion but BNP 26. She was continued on 
her home regimen of lasix and metoprolol.
  
# Tachycardia: Ongoing sinus tachycardia for years, continued on 
home regimen of metoprolol.  HR consistently 90-110s throughout 
admission.  
  
# EKG/Trops: Her trop and CKMB were elevated ___ her 
polymyositis as they have been in the past. Trop 0.18 and CKMB 
51 with an index of 1.4 all of which are consistent with her 
previous levels during flares, so levels were not trended.
